method: HOUSECARL_SKILL_AUTHORING.md §6.5 manual/fan-out validation (run_loop.py uses select(), broken on Windows per §6.4). Empirical step = independent fan-out of 20 fresh-context agents, one per query, each shown a neutral menu of 11 skill descriptions (dialogue-authoring at D among realistic siblings, NOT flagged as under-test; siblings shown with abridged faithful descriptions matching deployment) + one query, asked which ONE skill to load (or NONE) + reasoning. Anonymized per feedback_skill_trigger_eval_fanout; agents told to judge ONLY the menu, use no tools, ignore environment skills. Verdicts adjudicated from each agent's REASONING + pick. Menu: A=SkyPatcher edit-record-fields, B=SPID distribute-to-NPCs, C=KID keywords-to-items, D=dialogue-authoring author-DIAL/INFO [under test], E=mutagen-reference record-schema, F=papyrus-reference function-signatures, G=papyrus-optimization script-perf, H=facegen-diagnostics dark-face, I=crash-diagnostics crash-logs, J=conflict-resolution which-plugin-wins, K=modding-basics install/newcomer. Run 2026-06-20 against the as-drafted description (worktree claude/unit-e-dialogue-skill, pre-PR).

result.notes: Clean sweep. All 10 should-trigger picked D, each citing D's DISTINCTIVE hooks (the .seq, voice .fuz, dropped-line/DIAL-wins, conditions-not-order, graph validation) rather than the bare word 'dialogue' — the description's specific scope is doing the routing. All 10 should-not routed elsewhere; the four hardest near-misses held with explicit boundary reasoning: q14 (names INFO/DialogResponses) -> E (schema vs authoring), q17 (npc + talking) -> H (dialogue fires fine, symptom is the face), q18 (voice type + npcs) -> B (distribution to NPCs, not authoring dialogue), q19 (dialogue topic + winner) -> J (wants the override winner, not to author). q15 routed to G (papyrus-optimization) instead of predicted F (papyrus-reference) — a papyrus-skill-internal wobble, NOT a dialogue-authoring false-trigger; specificity unaffected. Every manual_predicted_trigger matched the measured trigger/skip verdict.
result.peer_review: Author prediction + 20 independent fresh-context agents (exceeds §6.5's 'one peer reviewer checks 3 random'). Aaron may spot-check any query.
result.carry_forward: DA-V1X-1: re-run on the next release that ships a Windows-compatible eval runner (run_loop.py select() fix), per §6.4. Re-measure on ANY description change per feedback_skill_trigger_eval_fanout.
result.stale: STALE as of 2026-07-27 (#275), NOT re-run. Two reasons this measurement no longer describes the shipped skill: (1) the description changed in d7835ff ('dropped-line' -> 'dropped-line or reordered'), and this file's own carry_forward plus HOUSECARL_SKILL_AUTHORING.md §6.5 step 6 require a re-measure on ANY description change; (2) the DOCTRINE several agents cited when picking D — the DIAL-wins-wholesale dropped-line model — was falsified by measurement in #275, so the reasoning recorded in the case notes is a historical observation, NOT guidance. Case notes are left VERBATIM as what the 2026-06-20 agents actually said; correcting doctrine inside an observation would attribute to that run a rationale it never gave and destroy its use as the baseline a re-run compares against. DEBT: re-run the fan-out against the current description.
